analysis: All four units are documentation-only changes (docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md). No executable code, authorization, encryption, attestation or wire-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The visible head excerpts of inference.md (lines 1641-2316) are unchanged surrounding text. The changed ranges (head 872-878, 1123-1183, 2098) describe: (1) out-of-order completed observations in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate, with freshness anchored to the newest observation; (2) three deadline-admission estimator corrections gated by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, with =0 restoring the previous estimators; (3) a code-map path update at line 2098. The serving-performance doc updates its date and states the estimator corrections need no timing-catalog entry and that calibratedPathProven still separates exactly two conversions. Security relevance is limited. The estimators affect availability and scheduling (first-token deadline admission), related to T-010/T-029 only indirectly. They do not touch the prefix cache (T-041), App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053), or key custody. The documented kill switch is an environment variable on the operator's own provider, so it is not a new trust boundary. Limits: the full patch text for the inference.md hunk at 1123-1183 was truncated (only the start was supplied), and the underlying Swift source (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, FirstTokenDeadlineAdmissionV2.swift, EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift) was not supplied. I therefore cannot verify that the code behaves as documented, for example that stale or out-of-order evidence cannot let a provider over-admit work or advertise inflated freshness to the coordinator. This is a documentation-accuracy question for any code-side review, not a finding here. Existing admission, memory and physical-capacity gates are described as unchanged.
